name: ml-interview
title: ML Research / Engineering Interview Concepts
description: Concept list for ML interviews (RL, LLMs, generative models, applied ML, general ML, linear algebra), reordered into a learning path. Goal: breadth and intuition, with the key equation for each topic.

tiers.core: Very likely asked. Know it cold: definition, why, key equation, 30-second interview answer.
tiers.solid: Know the idea, why it exists, and how it relates to neighbours.
tiers.aware: Be able to say what it is and when you'd use it in two sentences.

topics.title: Dot product
checkpoints: What does the dot product measure geometrically?
Why does attention use dot products between queries and keys?
topics.ref: 3Blue1Brown, Essence of Linear Algebra ch. 9

topics.title: Orthogonality
checkpoints: What does it mean for two vectors to be orthogonal, and what's special about an orthogonal matrix?
Why is orthogonal weight initialisation useful for deep or recurrent nets?
topics.ref: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra ch. 4

topics.title: Linear independence
checkpoints: Define linear independence.
What happens to linear regression when two features are perfectly collinear?
topics.ref: Strang ch. 3

topics.title: Rank / Span
checkpoints: What is the rank of a matrix, in words?
What is a low-rank matrix and why does LoRA assume weight updates are low rank?
topics.ref: Strang ch. 3

topics.title: Null space / Image space
checkpoints: What are the null space and image (column space) of A?
State the rank-nullity theorem.
topics.ref: Strang ch. 3

topics.title: Determinant
checkpoints: What does the determinant mean geometrically?
Where does a log-determinant show up in ML (hint: normalising flows / Gaussians)?
topics.ref: 3Blue1Brown, Essence of Linear Algebra ch. 6

topics.title: Singular matrices
checkpoints: Give three equivalent ways to say a square matrix is singular.
Why can X^T X be singular, and how does ridge regression fix it?
topics.ref: Strang ch. 5

topics.title: Inverse of a matrix
checkpoints: When does an inverse exist?
Why do we almost never explicitly compute a matrix inverse in numerical code?
topics.ref: Strang ch. 2

topics.title: Eigenvectors / Eigenvalues
checkpoints: Define an eigenvector and eigenvalue.
How do eigenvalues of the recurrent weight matrix relate to exploding/vanishing gradients in RNNs?
How does PCA use eigenvectors?
topics.ref: 3Blue1Brown, Essence of Linear Algebra ch. 14

topics.title: Positive semi-definite
checkpoints: Define a PSD matrix two ways (quadratic form, eigenvalues).
Why is every covariance matrix PSD?
What does a PSD Hessian tell you about a function?
topics.ref: Boyd & Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, appendix A

topics.title: Jacobian
checkpoints: What is the Jacobian of f: R^n -> R^m and what shape is it?
How does backprop relate to vector-Jacobian products?
topics.ref: Deep Learning (Goodfellow et al.) ch. 4 & 6.5

topics.title: Hessian
checkpoints: What is the Hessian and what does it tell you about curvature?
Why is computing the full Hessian impractical for neural nets?
topics.ref: Deep Learning (Goodfellow et al.) ch. 4.3

topics.title: PDF / PMF
checkpoints: What's the difference between a PDF and a PMF?
Can a PDF be greater than 1? Why?
topics.ref: Bishop, PRML ch. 1.2

topics.title: Expectation
checkpoints: Define expectation for discrete and continuous variables.
Why is linearity of expectation so useful, and does it need independence?
topics.ref: Bishop, PRML ch. 1.2.2

topics.title: Variance and covariance
checkpoints: Define variance and covariance.
Var(X + Y) = ? and when does it simplify?
Does zero covariance imply independence?
topics.ref: Bishop, PRML ch. 1.2.2

topics.title: Bayes' theorem
checkpoints: Write Bayes' theorem and name each term (prior, likelihood, posterior, evidence).
Classic: a test is 99% accurate for a disease with 1% prevalence. You test positive. Rough probability you have it?
topics.ref: Bishop, PRML ch. 1.2.3

topics.title: MLE vs MAP
checkpoints: Define MLE and MAP.
Show that MAP with a Gaussian prior gives L2 regularisation.
Why does minimising cross-entropy equal maximum likelihood?
topics.ref: Murphy, Probabilistic ML ch. 4

topics.title: Entropy
checkpoints: Define entropy and what it measures.
Which distribution over k outcomes has maximum entropy?
What is cross-entropy and how does it relate to entropy and KL?
topics.ref: Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory ch. 2

topics.title: KL divergence
checkpoints: Write KL(p||q). Is it symmetric? Is it a distance?
Forward vs reverse KL: which is mode-covering and which is mode-seeking?
Name three places KL appears in modern ML.
topics.ref: Murphy, Probabilistic ML ch. 6.2

topics.title: Jensen-Shannon divergence
checkpoints: Define JS divergence in terms of KL.
How does JS relate to the original GAN objective, and what goes wrong when supports don't overlap?
topics.ref: Goodfellow et al. 2014, GANs; Arjovsky et al. 2017, Wasserstein GAN

topics.title: Confidence intervals
checkpoints: What does a 95% confidence interval actually mean (and not mean)?
How would you put error bars on a model's accuracy on a test set of n examples?
topics.ref: Wasserman, All of Statistics ch. 6

topics.title: Supervised vs unsupervised
checkpoints: Define supervised, unsupervised and self-supervised learning with an example each.
Is LLM pretraining supervised or unsupervised? Defend your answer.
topics.ref: Murphy, Probabilistic ML ch. 1

topics.title: Linear regression
checkpoints: Write the least-squares loss and the closed-form solution.
What probabilistic assumption makes least squares the MLE?
When would you use gradient descent instead of the closed form?
topics.ref: Bishop, PRML ch. 3.1

topics.title: Loss functions
checkpoints: When would you use MSE vs MAE vs Huber?
Why cross-entropy rather than MSE for classification?
What's a hinge loss and where is it used?
topics.ref: Deep Learning (Goodfellow et al.) ch. 6.2

topics.title: Gradient descent / SGD
checkpoints: Write the GD update. What's different in SGD and mini-batch SGD?
Why does SGD noise sometimes help generalisation?
What happens if the learning rate is too high or too low?
topics.ref: Ruder 2016, An overview of gradient descent optimization algorithms

topics.title: Convex functions
checkpoints: Define a convex function.
Why does convexity matter for optimisation?
Is a neural network's loss convex in its weights? Why not?
topics.ref: Boyd & Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization ch. 3

topics.title: Newton's method
checkpoints: Write the Newton update for minimisation.
Why does it converge faster than GD near the optimum, and why don't we use it for big nets?
topics.ref: Nocedal & Wright, Numerical Optimization ch. 3

topics.title: Second-order methods
checkpoints: Name two practical second-order or quasi-second-order methods (e.g. L-BFGS, K-FAC, Shampoo) and the trick each uses.
What is a Hessian-vector product and why is it cheap?
topics.ref: Martens & Grosse 2015, K-FAC; Gupta et al. 2018, Shampoo

topics.title: Bias-variance tradeoff
checkpoints: Write the bias-variance decomposition of expected squared error.
How does model complexity move bias and variance?
What is double descent and how does it complicate the classical picture?
topics.ref: Hastie et al., Elements of Statistical Learning ch. 7; Belkin et al. 2019, Reconciling modern ML and the bias-variance trade-off

topics.title: Overfitting / underfitting
checkpoints: How do you diagnose overfitting vs underfitting from train/val curves?
List four things you'd try for each.
topics.ref: Deep Learning (Goodfellow et al.) ch. 5.2

topics.title: Regularisation methods
checkpoints: L1 vs L2: what does each do to weights and why does L1 give sparsity?
Name four regularisers used in deep learning.
How is weight decay different from L2 regularisation under Adam?
topics.ref: Deep Learning (Goodfellow et al.) ch. 7

topics.title: Cross validation
checkpoints: Describe k-fold cross-validation.
Why is a separate test set still needed? Give an example of leakage.
topics.ref: Hastie et al., ESL ch. 7.10

topics.title: Early stopping
checkpoints: How does early stopping work and why is it a regulariser?
Under what conditions is it roughly equivalent to L2 regularisation?
topics.ref: Deep Learning (Goodfellow et al.) ch. 7.8

topics.title: Precision / Recall / F1 / AUC-ROC
checkpoints: Define precision, recall and F1.
What does AUC-ROC measure, and why can it mislead on very imbalanced data (vs PR-AUC)?
For fraud detection, which would you optimise and why?
topics.ref: Davis & Goadrich 2006, The Relationship Between Precision-Recall and ROC Curves

topics.title: Curse of dimensionality
checkpoints: What goes wrong with distances in high dimensions?
Why does deep learning still work on high-dimensional inputs like images (manifold hypothesis)?
topics.ref: Bishop, PRML ch. 1.4

topics.title: No free lunch theorem
checkpoints: State the no free lunch theorem informally.
What's the practical takeaway (inductive bias)?
topics.ref: Wolpert & Macready 1997

topics.title: K-nearest neighbours
checkpoints: How does kNN classify, and how does k trade bias against variance?
Why is it slow at inference, and what's used to speed it up?
topics.ref: Hastie et al., ESL ch. 13

topics.title: Clustering (k-means etc.)
checkpoints: Describe Lloyd's algorithm for k-means. What does it minimise?
Name its failure modes and an alternative (GMM, DBSCAN) for each.
How do you pick k?
topics.ref: Bishop, PRML ch. 9

topics.title: SVMs
checkpoints: What is the max-margin idea and what are support vectors?
What is the kernel trick?
What is the soft-margin C parameter?
topics.ref: Bishop, PRML ch. 7

topics.title: Decision trees
checkpoints: How does a tree choose a split (Gini / entropy)?
Why do single trees overfit and how do you control it?
topics.ref: Hastie et al., ESL ch. 9.2

topics.title: Bagging
checkpoints: What is bootstrap aggregating and which error component does it reduce?
What does a random forest add on top of bagging?
topics.ref: Breiman 1996, Bagging Predictors; Breiman 2001, Random Forests

topics.title: Boosting
checkpoints: How does boosting differ from bagging, and which error component does it reduce?
Explain gradient boosting as gradient descent in function space.
Why are XGBoost/LightGBM still the default for tabular data?
topics.ref: Friedman 2001, Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine

topics.title: Ensembles
checkpoints: Why does averaging models help? When does it not help?
Name a deep-learning use of ensembles (e.g. uncertainty, model soups).
topics.ref: Lakshminarayanan et al. 2017, Deep Ensembles

topics.title: Dimensionality reduction
checkpoints: Explain PCA: what it maximises and how it's computed (SVD/eigen).
PCA vs t-SNE/UMAP: when would you use each?
topics.ref: Bishop, PRML ch. 12

topics.title: Data whitening
checkpoints: What does whitening do to the covariance of the data?
How is whitening different from standardisation, and why does preprocessing input scale help optimisation?
topics.ref: Kessy et al. 2018, Optimal Whitening and Decorrelation

topics.title: Backpropagation
checkpoints: Explain backprop as the chain rule over a computation graph.
Why is reverse-mode autodiff efficient for scalar losses with many parameters?
What has to be stored from the forward pass, and why does that dominate memory?
topics.ref: Karpathy, micrograd / 'Yes you should understand backprop'

topics.title: Activation functions
checkpoints: Why do we need non-linear activations?
Compare sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, GELU, SwiGLU: pros and cons.
What is a dead ReLU?
topics.ref: Shazeer 2020, GLU Variants Improve Transformer

topics.title: Weight initialisation
checkpoints: Why not initialise all weights to zero?
What's the idea behind Xavier/Glorot and He initialisation (keep variance constant across layers)?
topics.ref: Glorot & Bengio 2010; He et al. 2015, Delving Deep into Rectifiers

topics.title: Exploding / vanishing gradients
checkpoints: Why do gradients explode or vanish in deep nets / RNNs?
List five fixes and which problem each targets.
topics.ref: Pascanu et al. 2013, On the difficulty of training RNNs

topics.title: BatchNorm / LayerNorm / RMSNorm
checkpoints: What axis does BatchNorm normalise over vs LayerNorm?
Why do transformers use LayerNorm/RMSNorm instead of BatchNorm?
What does RMSNorm drop, and pre-norm vs post-norm: which is more stable?
topics.ref: Ioffe & Szegedy 2015; Ba et al. 2016; Zhang & Sennrich 2019, RMSNorm

topics.title: Adam / AdamW / Adagrad
checkpoints: Write Adam's update: what are m and v and why bias-correct?
What does AdamW change and why does it matter?
What problem did Adagrad have that RMSProp/Adam fixed?
topics.ref: Kingma & Ba 2014, Adam; Loshchilov & Hutter 2017, Decoupled Weight Decay

topics.title: CNNs
checkpoints: What inductive biases do convolutions encode?
Compute the output shape and parameter count of a conv layer.
What do residual connections fix (ResNet)?
topics.ref: He et al. 2015, Deep Residual Learning

topics.title: RNNs / LSTMs
checkpoints: How does an LSTM's cell state and gating help with vanishing gradients?
Why were RNNs replaced by transformers for language modelling?
topics.ref: Colah's blog, Understanding LSTM Networks

topics.title: Autoencoders
checkpoints: What is an autoencoder and what stops it learning the identity?
Name variants (denoising, sparse, masked) and what each is for.
topics.ref: He et al. 2021, Masked Autoencoders

topics.title: Gumbel-Softmax
checkpoints: What problem does Gumbel-Softmax solve (backprop through discrete sampling)?
What does the temperature do, and what's the straight-through variant?
topics.ref: Jang et al. 2016; Maddison et al. 2016, Concrete distribution

topics.title: Transfer learning
checkpoints: What is transfer learning and why does it work?
Feature extraction vs full fine-tuning: when to use each?
topics.ref: Yosinski et al. 2014, How transferable are features in deep neural networks?

topics.title: Few-shot / zero-shot learning
checkpoints: Define zero-shot and few-shot learning.
How does CLIP do zero-shot classification? How does GPT-3 do few-shot (in-context learning)?
topics.ref: Radford et al. 2021, CLIP; Brown et al. 2020, GPT-3

topics.title: Domain adaptation
checkpoints: What is distribution shift (covariate vs label shift)?
Name one domain adaptation technique (e.g. DANN, importance weighting).
topics.ref: Ganin et al. 2016, Domain-Adversarial Training

topics.title: Tokenisation
checkpoints: How does BPE build a vocabulary?
Why subword rather than characters or whole words?
Give two model failures caused by tokenisation.
topics.ref: Sennrich et al. 2016, BPE; Karpathy, 'Let's build the GPT Tokenizer'

topics.title: Causal (self-)attention
checkpoints: Write scaled dot-product attention.
How is the causal mask applied, and why is it needed for training?
What is the time and memory complexity in sequence length? What is a KV cache?
Why multiple heads?
topics.ref: Vaswani et al. 2017, Attention Is All You Need; Karpathy, 'Let's build GPT'

topics.title: Attention scaling factor (1/sqrt(d_k))
checkpoints: Why divide QK^T by sqrt(d_k)? Derive the variance argument.
What happens to softmax gradients if you don't?
topics.ref: Vaswani et al. 2017, section 3.2.1. (Deck note: 'LLM scaling factor' in the source list most likely means this; if it meant model scaling, see Scaling Laws.)

topics.title: Cross attention
checkpoints: How is cross attention different from self attention (where do Q, K, V come from)?
Give two places it's used (encoder-decoder translation, text-conditioning in diffusion).
topics.ref: Vaswani et al. 2017; Rombach et al. 2022, Latent Diffusion

topics.title: Sinusoidal positional embeddings
checkpoints: Why does a transformer need positional information at all?
How are sinusoidal embeddings built, and why multiple frequencies?
topics.ref: Vaswani et al. 2017, section 3.5

topics.title: Relative positional embeddings
checkpoints: Absolute vs relative positions: what's the motivation for relative?
Name two relative schemes (Shaw et al., T5 bias, ALiBi).
topics.ref: Shaw et al. 2018; Press et al. 2021, ALiBi

topics.title: RoPE
checkpoints: How does RoPE encode position (rotating q and k)?
Why does the q·k dot product then depend only on relative position?
How do context-extension tricks (position interpolation, NTK/YaRN) modify RoPE?
topics.ref: Su et al. 2021, RoFormer; EleutherAI blog on RoPE

topics.title: Flash Attention
checkpoints: What bottleneck does FlashAttention target (memory bandwidth, HBM vs SRAM)?
Explain tiling + online softmax in a few sentences.
Is it an approximation? What does it save in memory?
topics.ref: Dao et al. 2022, FlashAttention

topics.title: Transformer-XL
checkpoints: What is segment-level recurrence and what problem does it solve?
Why did it need relative positional encodings?
topics.ref: Dai et al. 2019, Transformer-XL

topics.title: Perceiver
checkpoints: How does the Perceiver avoid quadratic cost in input size (latent array + cross attention)?
Why is that useful for multimodal inputs?
topics.ref: Jaegle et al. 2021, Perceiver; Perceiver IO

topics.title: Mixture of Experts
checkpoints: How does a sparse MoE layer work (router, top-k experts)?
Why does it decouple parameter count from FLOPs per token?
What is load balancing and why is it needed?
topics.ref: Shazeer et al. 2017; Fedus et al. 2021, Switch Transformer; Mixtral 2024

topics.title: Scaling laws
checkpoints: What do scaling laws say about loss vs params, data and compute?
What did Chinchilla change about Kaplan's compute-optimal recipe (~20 tokens/param)?
Why do people train smaller models on far more tokens than Chinchilla-optimal?
topics.ref: Kaplan et al. 2020; Hoffmann et al. 2022, Chinchilla

topics.title: Pretraining
checkpoints: What is the pretraining objective of a decoder-only LLM?
What matters most in pretraining data and how is it filtered/deduplicated?
Rough FLOPs for training: 6 * N * D. Where does the 6 come from?
topics.ref: Radford et al. 2019, GPT-2; Llama 3 paper (data section)

topics.title: Finetuning (SFT / instruction tuning)
checkpoints: What is supervised fine-tuning and what data does it use?
What is catastrophic forgetting and how do you mitigate it?
Why mask the loss on prompt tokens?
topics.ref: Wei et al. 2021, FLAN; Ouyang et al. 2022, InstructGPT (SFT stage)

topics.title: LoRA
checkpoints: Write the LoRA update W + BA and give the shapes.
Why initialise B to zero? What does the alpha/r scaling do?
Why can LoRA weights be merged at inference with zero overhead? What's QLoRA?
topics.ref: Hu et al. 2021, LoRA; Dettmers et al. 2023, QLoRA

topics.title: Decoding techniques
checkpoints: Compare greedy, beam search, temperature, top-k and top-p (nucleus) sampling.
Why does beam search produce bland/repetitive text for open-ended generation?
What is speculative decoding and why is it lossless?
topics.ref: Holtzman et al. 2019, The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration; Leviathan et al. 2023, Speculative Decoding

topics.title: S4 (structured state space models)
checkpoints: What is a linear state space model and how can it be computed both as a recurrence and as a convolution?
What did Mamba add (input-dependent / selective parameters)?
topics.ref: Gu et al. 2021, S4; Gu & Dao 2023, Mamba; 'The Annotated S4'

topics.title: Griffin
checkpoints: What is Griffin's architecture (gated linear recurrence + local attention)?
What inference advantage does a fixed-size recurrent state give over a growing KV cache?
topics.ref: De et al. 2024, Griffin (Google DeepMind); RecurrentGemma

topics.title: Transformer vs RNN vs S4
checkpoints: Compare training parallelism, inference cost per token, memory and long-range recall for each.

topics.ref: Gu & Dao 2023, Mamba (related work section)

topics.title: Floating point representation
checkpoints: What are sign, exponent and mantissa?

Why is BF16 preferred over FP16 for training?
topics.ref: Kalamkar et al. 2019, A Study of BFLOAT16 for Deep Learning Training

topics.title: Numerical precision tricks
checkpoints: Explain log-sum-exp and the max-subtraction trick for softmax.
Why compute cross-entropy from logits rather than probabilities?
Where do you add epsilons and why?
topics.ref: Blanchard et al. 2019, Accurately computing the log-sum-exp and softmax functions

topics.title: Mixed precision training
checkpoints: What's kept in FP32 and what runs in FP16/BF16?
Why is loss scaling needed for FP16 but usually not BF16?
topics.ref: Micikevicius et al. 2017, Mixed Precision Training

topics.title: Gradient clipping
checkpoints: Clip by value vs clip by global norm: which is standard and why?
What do loss spikes in LLM training look like and how does clipping help?
topics.ref: Pascanu et al. 2013

topics.title: Gradient accumulation
checkpoints: How does gradient accumulation simulate a larger batch?
What must you be careful with (loss scaling by steps, BatchNorm stats)?
topics.ref: Hugging Face docs, 'Methods and tools for efficient training on a single GPU'

topics.title: Gradient checkpointing
checkpoints: What trade does activation checkpointing make?

topics.ref: Chen et al. 2016, Training Deep Nets with Sublinear Memory Cost

topics.title: Profiling
checkpoints: Your GPU utilisation is 40%. How do you find out why?
What is MFU and how do you estimate it?

topics.ref: PyTorch Profiler docs; Horace He, 'Making Deep Learning Go Brrrr From First Principles'

topics.title: JIT compiling
checkpoints: What does a JIT compiler (XLA, torch.compile) do to speed up a model (e.g. kernel fusion)?
What causes recompilation / graph breaks?
topics.ref: PyTorch 2 paper (Ansel et al. 2024); JAX docs on jit

topics.title: JAX vs PyTorch vs TensorFlow
checkpoints: Eager vs graph execution: where does each framework sit?
What are JAX's core transforms (jit, grad, vmap, pmap/shard_map) and its functional-purity constraint?
topics.ref: JAX docs, 'JAX: The Sharp Bits'

topics.title: Communication primitives
checkpoints: Define all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, broadcast.
Why is all-reduce = reduce-scatter + all-gather, and what does ring all-reduce cost?
topics.ref: NCCL docs, Collective Operations; Hugging Face 'Ultra-Scale Playbook'

topics.title: DDP (data parallel)
checkpoints: How does DDP work and which collective does it use?
How does it overlap communication with backward (gradient bucketing)?
What's DDP's memory limitation?
topics.ref: Li et al. 2020, PyTorch Distributed

topics.title: FSDP / ZeRO
checkpoints: What do ZeRO stages 1, 2, 3 shard?
Walk through FSDP's forward and backward: which collectives and when?
Compute the memory per parameter for mixed-precision Adam (~16 bytes) and how sharding divides it.
topics.ref: Rajbhandari et al. 2019, ZeRO; Zhao et al. 2023, PyTorch FSDP

topics.title: Tensor parallelism
checkpoints: How does Megatron split an MLP (column- then row-parallel) to need one all-reduce?
Why is TP usually kept within a node?
topics.ref: Shoeybi et al. 2019, Megatron-LM

topics.title: Pipeline parallelism
checkpoints: What is the pipeline bubble and how do micro-batches shrink it?

How do DP, TP and PP combine in 3D parallelism?

topics.title: VAEs and the ELBO

Why are VAE samples often blurry?

topics.title: GANs

What did WGAN change?
topics.ref: Goodfellow et al. 2014; Arjovsky et al. 2017, WGAN

topics.title: Score function
checkpoints: What is the score, grad_x log p(x), and why doesn't it need the normalising constant?

How does Langevin dynamics use the score to sample?
topics.ref: Song & Ermon 2019; Yang Song's blog, 'Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution'

topics.title: Diffusion forward process

How does rectified flow relate, and why is it used in recent image models?

topics.title: Exploration vs exploitation
checkpoints: Explain the dilemma with a bandit example.
Compare epsilon-greedy, UCB, Thompson sampling and entropy bonuses.
How is exploration handled when RL-tuning an LLM?
topics.ref: Sutton & Barto ch. 2; Lattimore & Szepesvari, Bandit Algorithms

topics.title: Credit assignment problem
checkpoints: What is temporal credit assignment?
Which tools address it (discounting, value functions/bootstrapping, GAE, reward shaping)?
Why is it hard for LLM reasoning with only a final-answer reward?
topics.ref: Minsky 1961; Sutton & Barto ch. 12

topics.title: Importance sampling
checkpoints: Write the importance sampling estimator E_p[f] = E_q[(p/q) f].
Why does variance blow up when p and q differ, especially over long trajectories?
Where does the ratio show up in PPO?
topics.ref: Sutton & Barto ch. 5.5

topics.title: Policy gradient theorem
checkpoints: Write the REINFORCE gradient: E[grad log pi(a|s) * G].
Explain the log-derivative trick.
Why doesn't the gradient need the derivative of the environment dynamics?
topics.ref: Sutton et al. 2000; Lilian Weng, 'Policy Gradient Algorithms'

topics.title: Variance reduction in RL
checkpoints: Why can you subtract a baseline without biasing the gradient?
Name three variance-reduction techniques (baseline, reward-to-go, advantage/critic, larger batches).
What's the bias-variance trade-off of using a learned critic?
topics.ref: Greensmith et al. 2004; Schulman et al. 2015, GAE (intro)

topics.title: Actor-critic
checkpoints: What do the actor and critic each learn?
What is the advantage A(s,a) and why use it instead of the return?
What is A2C/A3C?
topics.ref: Mnih et al. 2016, A3C; Sutton & Barto ch. 13.5

topics.title: GAE (generalized advantage estimation)
checkpoints: Write GAE as a discounted sum of TD errors delta_t.
What do lambda = 0 and lambda = 1 correspond to?
Which way does lambda move bias and variance?
topics.ref: Schulman et al. 2015, High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using GAE

topics.title: PPO
checkpoints: Write the clipped surrogate objective and explain each term.
Why clip? What failure of vanilla policy gradient does it prevent (and how does TRPO solve the same problem)?
What are the parts of the full PPO loss (policy, value, entropy) and the training loop?
topics.ref: Schulman et al. 2017, PPO; 'The 37 Implementation Details of PPO' (ICLR blog track)

topics.title: Soft Actor-Critic
checkpoints: What is the maximum-entropy RL objective?
Why is SAC off-policy and sample efficient, and what's the temperature alpha?
Why two Q networks?
topics.ref: Haarnoja et al. 2018, Soft Actor-Critic

topics.title: Model-based vs model-free
checkpoints: Define both and give an example algorithm of each.
Why is model-based more sample efficient, and what's model bias / compounding error?
topics.ref: Moerland et al. 2020, Model-based RL: A Survey

topics.title: AlphaGo / AlphaZero
checkpoints: How do policy network, value network and MCTS fit together?
What did AlphaZero remove compared to AlphaGo (human data) and why does self-play work?
What is PUCT in MCTS?
topics.ref: Silver et al. 2016, AlphaGo; Silver et al. 2017, AlphaGo Zero

topics.title: MuZero
checkpoints: What does MuZero learn instead of the true environment rules (representation, dynamics, prediction functions)?
Why doesn't its model need to reconstruct observations?
topics.ref: Schrittwieser et al. 2020, MuZero

topics.title: World Models / Dreamer
checkpoints: What does it mean to learn behaviour 'in imagination'?
What are Dreamer's main parts (RSSM world model, actor, critic trained on imagined rollouts)?
Contrast with MuZero's value-equivalent model.
topics.ref: Ha & Schmidhuber 2018, World Models; Hafner et al. 2023, DreamerV3

topics.title: Curriculum learning
checkpoints: What is curriculum learning and why can it help?
Give an RL example (automatic curricula, self-play, difficulty filtering of prompts in LLM RL).
topics.ref: Bengio et al. 2009, Curriculum Learning

topics.title: RLHF
checkpoints: Walk through the three stages (SFT, reward model, RL).
How is the reward model trained (Bradley-Terry on pairwise preferences)?
Why the KL penalty to the reference model? What is reward hacking?
topics.ref: Ouyang et al. 2022, InstructGPT; Nathan Lambert, 'RLHF Book'

topics.title: DPO (Direct Preference Optimisation)
checkpoints: Write the DPO loss.
What's the key insight (closed-form optimal policy of KL-regularised RL, so the reward is implicit)?
Pros and cons vs PPO-based RLHF?
topics.ref: Rafailov et al. 2023, Direct Preference Optimization

topics.title: GRPO
checkpoints: How does GRPO compute advantages without a critic (group-relative normalisation)?
Why is that attractive for LLMs with verifiable rewards?
What are known issues and fixes (length bias, std normalisation; e.g. Dr. GRPO, DAPO)?
topics.ref: Shao et al. 2024, DeepSeekMath; DeepSeek-AI 2025, DeepSeek-R1
